target.title: fix(discord): limit implicit reply references to first chunk
target.body:
Closes #99068

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with `replyToMode: "first"` could receive one native reply notification per physical chunk when a single long agent reply was split into multiple Discord messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now carries a source-aware first-chunk-only flag from outbound delivery into the shared send layer. The flag is only enabled for implicit single-use reply targets, so explicit `[[reply_to_*]]` replies and all-mode replies keep their existing reusable native reply behavior while the implicit turn reply no longer fans out across every physical text or media-caption chunk.

The payload send path now uses the same reply fanout contract for each physical Discord send, including `audioAsVoice`, native Discord payload media, and component follow-up media. That closes the reviewer-noted gap where one captured implicit reply id could be reused across voice/text/media sends.

The related open PR #99083 is not a strong blocker for this replacement shape: its current live review is still `status: needs proof` / `rating: unranked`, and ClawSweeper found that its mode-only suppression can break explicit first-mode chunk replies. This PR uses the reply source to avoid that compatibility regression.

## User Impact

Long Discord replies in first/batched implicit reply modes now quote the source message only on the first physical Discord message, avoiding repeated reply notifications for one logical answer. Explicit reply tags and all-mode replies remain reusable across chunks and payload sends as before.

## Evidence

- Claim proved on current head `71ae6b987eb7b5124e8921f7789ff96b865986ba`: Discord request bodies only include `message_reference` on the first physical chunk when the reply target is implicit single-use, while direct/default sends, explicit replies, and `replyToMode: "all"` keep their reusable native reply behavior.
- Claim proved on current head: the `audioAsVoice` payload path no longer captures and reuses one implicit reply id across voice/text/media physical sends; the regression now expects the voice send to keep the single implicit reply and the later text/media sends to omit it.
- Claim proved on current head: native Discord payload media sends propagate `replyToFirstChunkOnly: true` for implicit first-mode sends, so a direct payload send that internally chunks still suppresses trailing chunk native references.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-plan.test.ts --reporter=verbose` passed: 3 files, 89 tests.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-send-context.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mjs --mode=src-outside-plugin-sdk` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` exited 0 with no actionable output.

Not tested / proof gaps:

- I did not run a live Discord bot/channel scenario in this checkout because the local environment has no Discord bot token or channel id available (`DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_DISCORD_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_LIVE_DISCORD_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID`, and `DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` were all absent; no secret values were printed). The current proof exercises the real Discord send serialization boundary used by `createChannelMessage`, but it does not visually prove Discord client notification behavior.
- Requested live proof path: a maintainer/Mantis Discord run should verify that `replyToMode: "first"` quotes only the first long-reply chunk, while explicit first/all chunk replies keep expected native references.
